extras.workflow_content:
name: Deploy to Azure

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:

env:
  AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME: openai-cs-agents-backend
  AZURE_WEBAPP_PACKAGE_PATH: './python-backend'
  PYTHON_VERSION: '3.11'
  NODE_VERSION: '20'
  RESOURCE_GROUP: openai-cs-agents-demo-rg
  LOCATION: eastus2
  APP_SERVICE_PLAN: openai-cs-agents-plan
  STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME: openai-cs-agents-frontend

jobs:
  build-and-deploy-backend:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: ${{ env.PYTHON_VERSION }}

      - name: Install dependencies
        working-directory: ./python-backend
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install -r requirements.txt

      - name: Login to Azure
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Create Resource Group (if not exists)
        run: |
          az group create --name ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} --location ${{ env.LOCATION }} || true

      - name: Create App Service Plan (Free Tier)
        run: |
          az appservice plan create \
            --name ${{ env.APP_SERVICE_PLAN }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --sku F1 \
            --is-linux || true

      - name: Create Web App
        run: |
          az webapp create \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --plan ${{ env.APP_SERVICE_PLAN }} \
            --runtime "PYTHON:3.11" || true

      - name: Configure App Settings
        run: |
          az webapp config appsettings set \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --settings \
              OPENAI_API_KEY="${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}" \
              SCM_DO_BUILD_DURING_DEPLOYMENT=true \
              WEBSITES_PORT=8000

      - name: Configure startup command
        run: |
          az webapp config set \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --startup-file "gunicorn -w 2 -k uvicorn.workers.UvicornWorker api:app --bind 0.0.0.0:8000"

      - name: Deploy to Azure Web App
        uses: azure/webapps-deploy@v3
        with:
          app-name: ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }}
          package: ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_PACKAGE_PATH }}

      - name: Output Backend URL
        id: backend-url
        run: |
          BACKEND_URL="https://${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }}.azurewebsites.net"
          echo "BACKEND_URL=$BACKEND_URL" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "Backend deployed to: $BACKEND_URL"

    outputs:
      backend_url: ${{ steps.backend-url.outputs.BACKEND_URL }}

  build-and-deploy-frontend:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: build-and-deploy-backend
    
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}

      - name: Install pnpm
        run: npm install -g pnpm

      - name: Install dependencies
        working-directory: ./ui
        run: pnpm install

      - name: Build frontend
        working-directory: ./ui
        run: pnpm run build
        env:
          NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE: ${{ needs.build-and-deploy-backend.outputs.backend_url }}

      - name: Login to Azure
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Create Static Web App (if not exists)
        run: |
          az staticwebapp create \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --location ${{ env.LOCATION }} \
            --sku Free || true

      - name: Get Static Web App deployment token
        id: swa-token
        run: |
          TOKEN=$(az staticwebapp secrets list \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --query "properties.apiKey" -o tsv)
          echo "::add-mask::$TOKEN"
          echo "DEPLOYMENT_TOKEN=$TOKEN" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Deploy to Azure Static Web Apps
        uses: Azure/static-web-apps-deploy@v1
        with:
          azure_static_web_apps_api_token: ${{ steps.swa-token.outputs.DEPLOYMENT_TOKEN }}
          repo_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          action: "upload"
          app_location: "./ui/out"
          output_location: ""
          skip_app_build: true

      - name: Output Frontend URL
        run: |
          FRONTEND_URL=$(az staticwebapp show \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --query "defaultHostname" -o tsv)
          echo "Frontend deployed to: https://$FRONTEND_URL"

  configure-cors:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [build-and-deploy-backend, build-and-deploy-frontend]
    
    steps:
      - name: Login to Azure
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Get Static Web App URL
        id: frontend-url
        run: |
          FRONTEND_URL=$(az staticwebapp show \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --query "defaultHostname" -o tsv)
          echo "FRONTEND_URL=https://$FRONTEND_URL" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Configure CORS on Backend
        run: |
          FRONTEND_URL="${{ steps.frontend-url.outputs.FRONTEND_URL }}"
          # Pass ALLOWED_ORIGINS to FastAPI's CORSMiddleware via app setting.
          # Do NOT use `az webapp cors add` together with FastAPI's own CORSMiddleware —
          # both would add Access-Control-Allow-Origin headers, causing duplicate-header
          # rejections in browsers.  FastAPI's middleware is the single source of truth.
          az webapp config appsettings set \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --settings ALLOWED_ORIGINS="$FRONTEND_URL,http://localhost:3250,http://localhost:3000"
          # Clear any previously-added Azure-level CORS origins to avoid conflicts.
          az webapp cors remove \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --allowed-origins "*" || true

      - name: Summary
        run: |
          echo "=== Deployment Complete ==="
          echo "Backend URL: ${{ needs.build-and-deploy-backend.outputs.backend_url }}"
          echo "Frontend URL: ${{ steps.frontend-url.outputs.FRONTEND_URL }}"

summary.iac_security_summary:
# AI Application Infrastructure Security Briefing

## 1. Deployment Posture
- **Cloud provider:** Azure (single-region, no availability zones detected)
- **Deployment tool:** GitHub Actions with `ubuntu-latest` runners
- **High availability / resilience:** Not configured — no AZs, multi-region, or redundancy detected
- **Workflow triggers:** `push` and `workflow_dispatch` (any branch push triggers deployment)

## 2. Secret Management
- **Secret store:** `github_actions_secret` (GitHub encrypted secrets)
- **Risks:** Secret `AZURE_CREDENTIALS` is passed as plaintext workflow variable (`${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}`) into GitHub Actions runtime — exposed in logs if debug enabled, or via workflow artifact inspection
- **No OIDC:** long-lived static credentials used instead of short-lived tokens

## 3. Encryption
- **Encryption at rest:** Not configured — `encryption_at_rest_coverage: false`
- **Key management:** No customer-managed keys (CMK) detected; likely using Azure default platform-managed keys (PMK)

## 4. IAM / Least-Privilege
- **IAM type:** Managed Identity (Azure AD), scoped at **subscription** level — highly permissive
- **Trust principal:** GitHub Actions (no OIDC validation); any workflow can impersonate
- **Principal object:** `${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}` — single service principal with subscription-wide access
- **Risk:** No narrow scoping (e.g., resource group or specific RBAC role); full subscription access violates least-privilege

## 5. CI/CD Security
- **Runners:** `ubuntu-latest` — mutable, public Microsoft-hosted; no hardened/self-hosted runners
- **OIDC:** Not used (`uses_oidc: false`) — static credentials increase secret rotation burden and exposure window
- **Workflow trigger surface:** Any `push` to any branch triggers deployment; `workflow_dispatch` allows manual triggered deploys from any user with write access

## 6. Container Security
- No container-specific findings provided — assume no health checks, resource limits, or root-user restrictions enforced

## 7. Key Risks & Recommendations

### Priority 1: Replace static credentials with OIDC
- **Risk:** Long-lived `AZURE_CREDENTIALS` secret with subscription-wide scope; exposed to all workflow runs
- **Action:** Configure GitHub Actions OIDC trust with Azure AD + Federated Identity Credentials; restrict trust to specific repo, environment, and branch

### Priority 2: Restrict IAM scope
- **Risk:** Managed identity scoped at **subscription** level — any compromise grants full subscription access
- **Action:** Create resource-group-scoped managed identity with minimal RBAC role (e.g., Contributor on specific RG only); use separate identities per environment

### Priority 3: Harden CI/CD pipeline
- **Risk:** `push` trigger on any branch enables unauthorised deploys; `ubuntu-latest` runners lack isolation
- **Action:** Restrict workflow triggers to specific branches (e.g., `main`, `release/*`); use self-hosted or hardened runners with short-lived tokens; enable OIDC plus branch/ref validation in Azure AD trust policy

**Additional actions:**
- Enable encryption at rest with CMK (Azure Key Vault)
- Rotate static secrets immediately if they exist
- Add container health checks and resource limits at deployment level

relationship_graph_md:
## Component Relationship Graph

- **Entry Points & Auth:** FastAPI exposes endpoints (Login, Me, Logout, Chat). Bearer Auth protects all endpoints.
- **Guardrails:** Relevance and Jailbreak guardrails both use gpt-4.1-mini to filter requests, but they only apply to the Chat endpoint—no guardrail coverage shown for other endpoints.
- **Agent Orchestration:** The Triage Agent delegates to Flight Status, FAQ, Cancellation, and Seat Booking agents. All agents (including Triage) call the same five tools: Baggage, Cancel Flight, Display Seat Map, Faq Lookup, Flight Status.
- **Framework-Level Access:** OpenAI Agents framework directly calls all five tools plus Lookup Reservation and Update Seat, potentially bypassing agent-level logic.
- **Tool Risk:** All tools are reachable by multiple agents and the framework. No tool-level authorization or per-agent restrictions are indicated—any agent can call any tool.
- **Data Stores:** Sqlite datastore has no connections shown—its access path is unclear. No mention of encryption or access control for stored data.
- **Model Usage:** All agents and both guardrails rely on a single model (gpt-4.1-mini), creating a single point of failure for reasoning and safety.
